summary.intent: Determine whether the callisto repo has the same stale `orin-axi` remote reference that caused michi's Entire checkpoint push to hit the old org location.
summary.outcome: Confirmed callisto's `origin`, git config and `.entire/settings.json` already point to `orin-dx`; the only leftover is a released CHANGELOG example. Also clarified that michi's actual rejection was GitHub push protection catching an npm token in a checkpoint transcript, which a remote URL fix won't resolve.

repo: Callisto's `origin` is `git@github.com:orin-dx/callisto.git`; no `url.*` rewrites or `.entire/settings.json` entries reference `orin-axi`.
Entire pushes checkpoint refs (`refs/entire/checkpoints/...`) to `origin`, so they follow the remote's URL.
Callisto has about 8,687 local Entire checkpoint refs.
Michi's remote needs updating to `git@github.com:orin-dx/michi.git`; it still points to `orin-axi/michi`, which GitHub redirects with a 'repository moved' message.

code.finding: Only remaining `orin-axi` mention: uses `npm/@orin-axi/michi` as an example package name in an already-released entry; it is text, not a push target, so it was left as is.

workflow: Entire checkpoint transcripts (`full.jsonl`) can capture secrets printed during a session, such as npm tokens, and GitHub push protection will reject the checkpoint ref push.
A push failure can have two independent causes: a stale remote location (a warning) and secret scanning (the actual rejection). Fixing one does not fix the other.
Leaked tokens found in transcripts should be revoked, since they persist in local checkpoint data.
In this environment the sandbox blocked querying the remote, so only local state could be inspected.

friction: The sandbox blocked the query of the remote, so callisto's remote checkpoint state couldn't be verified.
The michi error output mixed a 'repository moved' notice with a secret-scanning rejection, making the root cause easy to misread.
open_items: Update michi's origin: `git -C <michi> remote set-url origin git@github.com:orin-dx/michi.git`.
Remove the npm token from michi's checkpoint commit f89c2e66 (`0/full.jsonl` lines 23363 and 23372) or allow it via the unblock URL, and revoke that npm token.
Optionally scan callisto's local checkpoint transcripts for npm/GitHub token patterns; offered but not done.
